title: Characterizing CSP languages with linear non-redundancy
formal: Characterize all finite constraint languages \(\Gamma\) over arbitrary finite nonempty domains for which every \(n\)-variable formula has a subformula with at most \(C_\Gamma n\) constraints and exactly the same set of satisfying assignments, for some constant \(C_\Gamma\) independent of the formula and \(n\). Equivalently, determine the class-membership function \(\chi_{\mathrm{lin}}\) on all such finite languages, taking value \(1\) when this property holds and \(0\) otherwise. The target is the full classification from Question 8; it is not restricted to Boolean domains or to a proposed sufficient condition.
why: A full classification would explain which systems of local relations always have a linear-sized exact description using their own constraints. It would organize connections among logical redundancy, sparsification, preprocessing and algebra across all finite domains. The distinction between existence of a small subformula and efficiently finding it is essential to interpreting the result.
status_note: Question 8 in the July 2024 workshop source poses the full classification. The December 2025 Richness revision and May 2026 shrinking manuscript retain it, and the published July 2026 arity-four paper gives only a restricted near-classification. These primary sources were checked on 15 September 2026; bounded later-work searches did not find a full resolution. Proofs and computational classifications were not independently reproduced.

progress.text: Chen, Jansen and Pieterse establish ring-based linear sparsification results for Boolean languages and classifications in important restricted cases.
Carbonnel develops an algebraic framework for non-redundancy and characterizes when the trivial maximal-arity bound is tight.
PACS Question 8 asks for the full linear classification and distinguishes the Boolean candidate condition from the general finite-domain problem.
The revised Richness manuscript relates Boolean Mal’tsev embeddings to balanced relations and explicitly leaves the complete linear classification open.
The shrinking-instances manuscript advances superlinear lower bounds and again identifies the linear or near-linear classification as open.
The CP 2026 paper gives a near-complete four-ary Boolean classification, including non-polynomial asymptotics and one remaining predicate; this is a restricted-domain result.

sentences: Non-redundancy measures how many constraints can remain individually essential in a formula.
The question asks which finite languages always allow a subformula with linearly many constraints and the identical set of satisfying assignments.
The number of variables is the size parameter, and the linear constant may depend on the language.
The classification includes all finite domains and does not require an efficient algorithm to find the subformula.
A solution would identify the structural boundary for compact exact descriptions of constraint systems.

definitions:
A language \(\Gamma\) consists of a finite nonempty domain \(D=\{1,\ldots,d\}\) and a finite list of named relations \(R\subseteq D^{r}\), each with a positive integer arity \(r\). Empty and full relations, and the empty list of relations, are permitted. The domain, arities and relation tables give the entire description. A formula \(F\) on variables \(V=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), \(n\geq1\), is a finite conjunction of constraints \(R(x_1,\ldots,x_{r})\) from this language. Variable repetitions and repeated constraints are permitted. An assignment \(a:V\to D\) satisfies the constraint when \((a(x_1),\ldots,a(x_{r}))\in R\), and satisfies \(F\) when it satisfies every constraint. Write \(\operatorname{Sol}_{D}(F)\subseteq D^{V}\) for this set; it may be empty.

A subformula \(F'\subseteq F\) is obtained only by deleting constraint occurrences, keeping the same variables and domain. It may have isolated variables and no constraints. The preservation requirement is \(\operatorname{Sol}_{D}(F')=\operatorname{Sol}_{D}(F)\), as sets of assignments on the original \(V\). It is stronger than merely preserving whether a satisfying assignment exists. No new constraints, new variables, weights or relaxation of relations are allowed.

Define
\[\operatorname{nr}_\Gamma(n)=\max_{F}\ \min_{\substack{F'\subseteq F\\\operatorname{Sol}_{D}(F')=\operatorname{Sol}_{D}(F)}} |F'|,\]
where \(F\) ranges over all formulas on these \(n\) variables and \(|F'|\) counts constraint occurrences. This maximum is finite: duplicate occurrences do not change solutions, and there are at most \(\sum_{R\in\Gamma}n^{\operatorname{arity}(R)}\) distinct constraints. An equivalent definition is the maximum size of a formula in which every constraint is non-redundant. A constraint \(C\) is non-redundant when there is an assignment satisfying all other constraints but violating \(C\). Unsatisfiable formulas are included; no satisfiability promise is made.

The numerical function being classified is
\[\chi_{\mathrm{lin}}(\Gamma)=\begin{cases}1,&\exists C\in\mathbb N_{\geq1}\ \forall n\geq1:\ \operatorname{nr}_\Gamma(n)\leq Cn,\\0,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}\]
Its domain consists of every finite language just defined, with no global bound on domain size, arity or number of relations. The hidden constant may depend on the whole fixed language. Requiring the bound at all positive \(n\) is equivalent to asymptotic \(O(n)\), since finitely many exceptions can be absorbed in the constant. A bound of \(n\log n\) or \(n^{1+o(1)}\) does not meet it.

This is a mathematical classification of an extremal property. No polynomial-time procedure for finding \(F'\), recognizing languages, or deciding satisfiability is built into the target. A structural criterion or another substantive unambiguous mathematical description of the membership function can specify an answer without a predetermined syntactic form. Introducing the characteristic function records the same classification target, rather than replacing it with an optimal-growth problem for \(\operatorname{nr}_\Gamma\).
answer_criterion: Supply a real-valued function \(g\) on the stated full domain and a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean that \(|g(\Gamma)-\chi_{\mathrm{lin}}(\Gamma)|\leq1/100\) for every finite language \(\Gamma\). An exact necessary-and-sufficient characterization of class membership also qualifies. The supplied description must determine membership substantively; merely renaming the defining optimization or repeating that a language is linear exactly when it has linear non-redundancy is not an answer. No efficient recognition algorithm is required. Prove both membership and nonmembership sides of the characterization, including all domains and arities. A sufficient algebraic condition, a finite table of small languages, a near-linear bound or a decision-preserving kernel alone does not settle the full target.

source_formulation.text: Which finite constraint languages allow every formula to be reduced to linearly many of its own constraints while preserving all satisfying assignments?
source_formulation.caption: Editorial paraphrase of PACS 2024 Question 8

context_blocks.text: A constraint can be logically unnecessary even when its relation occurs many times. For example, equality constraints connecting a set of variables can often be deleted while preserving the same equality requirements on all assignments. Non-redundancy asks how large a collection can remain when every member has its own witness to being essential.

This is a question about the amount of information in a system, not the difficulty of finding a satisfying assignment. Some NP-hard fixed predicates have linear non-redundancy. Conversely, the binary positive-OR relation has quadratic non-redundancy despite the simplicity of deciding its satisfiability. These contrasting examples separate this classification from the usual tractability dichotomy.

The 2020 Boolean work supplies linear sparsification through representations by degree-one equations over integer rings. The December 2025 manuscript identifies the Boolean languages admitting the more general Mal’tsev embedding condition with the corresponding balanced class, while exhibiting genuinely noncommutative behavior on larger domains. This clarifies known sufficient conditions without proving that they capture all languages with linear non-redundancy.

The 2025 manuscript realizes every rational non-redundancy exponent at least one over suitable finite domains. The resulting range is much richer than a choice between linear growth and the trivial maximal-arity bound. It does not supply a complete description of the languages at the linear endpoint.
The 2026 shrinking paper develops further superlinear lower bounds while retaining the general linear or near-linear classification as an open question.
The CP 2026 paper almost classifies Boolean arity four, leaving one predicate unresolved and exhibiting non-polynomial asymptotics. This is a restricted family within the all-language target.
